title: Octal Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert between decimal and octal, with binary and hex equivalents. Enter your convert and number and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Octal is base 8: it uses the digits 0–7, and each octal digit stands for exactly three binary bits. It was the standard way to write machine values on early computers (a 12-bit word is four octal digits), and it still appears in Unix file permissions — 755 means read-write-execute for the owner and read-execute for everyone else. This calculator converts both ways between decimal and octal, and shows the binary and hexadecimal equivalents too.

## How to use the Octal Calculator

Start by choosing your convert from the list, then entering your number. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Choose the direction: decimal to octal, or octal to decimal.
2. Enter the number — octal input may only contain the digits 0–7.
3. Read the result in octal, decimal, hexadecimal and binary.

## Formula

Decimal to octal: repeatedly divide by 8 and read the remainders bottom-up. Octal to decimal: multiply each digit by 8 raised to its position from the right, starting at 0.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 83 in decimal is 123 in octal (83 ÷ 8 = 10 remainder 3; 10 ÷ 8 = 1 remainder 2; 1 ÷ 8 = 0 remainder 1; read the remainders upwards: 123). The other way, 123 octal = 1×64 + 2×8 + 3 = 83. Try the same figures in the [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Convert: Decimal → Octal, Number: 83), the [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) returns Octal: 123, Decimal: 83, Hexadecimal: 0x53, Binary: 1010011. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Octal and Unix permissions

Unix file permissions are three octal digits: owner, group and others. Each digit is the sum of read (4), write (2) and execute (1), so 7 means read-write-execute, 5 means read-execute and 6 means read-write. That is why you see chmod 755 and chmod 644 so often: 755 is full access for the owner and read-execute for everyone else, and 644 is read-write for the owner and read-only for everyone else.

## Why octal groups three bits

Because 8 is 2³, each octal digit maps to exactly three binary digits: 0 = 000, 7 = 111. That made octal a compact way to write binary on machines with 12-, 24- or 36-bit words. Hexadecimal (base 16) does the same with four bits per digit and has mostly replaced octal today — except in permissions, where the three-bit grouping matches the read-write-execute pattern exactly.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Octal digits are only 0–7: 8 and 9 never appear in a valid octal number.
- To read a Unix permission, split it into three digits and add 4 + 2 + 1 for each.
- For base conversions in general, use the binary or hexadecimal converters too.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is octal?

A base-8 number system using the digits 0–7. Each octal digit represents three binary bits, which made it popular on early computers and keeps it alive in Unix file permissions. Try it with your own numbers in the [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How do I convert decimal to octal?

Divide by 8 repeatedly and read the remainders from bottom to top. 83 ÷ 8 leaves 3, 10 ÷ 8 leaves 2, 1 ÷ 8 leaves 1 — so 83 decimal is 123 octal. Try it with your own numbers in the [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What does chmod 755 mean?

Owner: 7 (read + write + execute), group: 5 (read + execute), others: 5 (read + execute). It is the standard permission for executable files and scripts. Try it with your own numbers in the [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Octal Calculator use?

Decimal to octal: repeatedly divide by 8 and read the remainders bottom-up. Octal to decimal: multiply each digit by 8 raised to its position from the right, starting at 0. You can see it in action in the [Octal Calculator](/octal-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
